newsitem.title: POLAND: FOUR YOUNG POLES JAILED FOR KILLING STUDENT.
newsitem.headline: FOUR YOUNG POLES JAILED FOR KILLING STUDENT.

text.p: Four young Poles in their early 20s, including a woman, were sentenced to jail terms of nine to 11 years on Monday for killing a medical student, PAP news agency said.
Ireneusz Reglinski, 21, was attacked in February 1996 by five drunken hooligans who pushed him out of a speeding commuter train in the Baltic port of Gdansk.
The student, who was killed instantly, also pulled one of the attackers with him who died as a result of inujuries.
Thousands of young people took to the streets of Gdansk in protest against the killing and the general wave of violence sweeping the country.
Seven friends of the hooligans, who testified as witnesses, are now on trial for perjury and could face up to five years in jail, PAP said.
They blamed the deceased attacker for Reglinski's death and frequently changed their testimony, greatly complicating the court's proceedings.
